q: Who called the Indian Constitution as "Quasi-Federal"?

options: The Indian State does not have any religious basis
There are no differences based on caste and religion
key_text: The Indian State does not have any religious basis

q: Important components of secularism in Constitution are mentioned in the below given statements. Find out the incorrect statement?
options: Prohibition against discrimination on ground of religion, caste etc
Sentiments of the majority people towards cow and against its slaughter
Secularism is not applicable to irreligious persons/citizens
key_text: Sentiments of the majority people towards cow and against its slaughter
explanation: Equality (Art. 14) and non-discrimination on religion (Art. 15) are components of secularism; the majority's sentiment about the cow (Art. 48, a DPSP on agriculture and animal husbandry) is not. exam: APPSC Asst. Engineers in AP Public Health & Municipal Engine
q: The words "Unity of the Nation" were added in the Preamble of Indian Constitution by which Amendment of the Constitution?
explanation: Strictly, 'unity of the Nation' was in the original 1949 Preamble; the 42nd Amendment (1976) changed it to 'unity and integrity of the Nation'. The question refers to that change, so the 42nd is the intended and only defensible option.

notes.text: - **Integrity** was **not** in the Preamble in **1975**; it came in **1976** (SSC 2019; UPPSC 2006). The word **"unity"** was in the **original** text – only "and integrity" was added (a question saying "'Unity of the Nation' was added by the 42nd" means this change).
